chunks: The eminent Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhayna, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:
When the sun passes its zenith, the gates of heaven and the gates of Paradise are opened, and supplications are answered. So blessed is the one for whom a righteous deed is raised at that time.

key_terms.أبواب الجنان: Gates of Paradise: The entrances to the gardens of the afterlife
key_terms.أبواب السماء: Gates of heaven: The metaphysical gateways through which prayers ascend
key_terms.استجيب الدعاء: Supplications are answered: Divine acceptance of prayers at this blessed hour
key_terms.زالت الشمس: Zawal al-shams: When the sun passes its zenith (midday), marking the beginning of Dhuhr prayer time
key_terms.طوبى: Tuba: Blessedness, felicity; also the name of a tree in Paradise

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of zawal time (when the sun passes its zenith) in Islam?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW), as narrated through Imam al-Baqir (AS), taught that the time of zawal (when the sun passes its zenith, marking the onset of Dhuhr prayer time) is a spiritually significant moment when the gates of heaven and Paradise open and supplications are accepted. This teaching was delivered to encourage believers to perform good deeds and supplicate at this blessed time, which was widely understood among early Muslims as the prime time for the noon prayer and supplication.

en.bilal-muhammad: Abu Ja`far Muhammad b. `Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babuwayh al-Qummi (ra) narrated to us. He said: My father (ra) narrated to us. He said: Sa`d b. `Abdullah narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. `Isa from al-Husayn b. Sa`id from Muhammad b. Abi `Umayr from `Umar b. Udhayna from Zurara from Abi Ja`far al-Baqir (as). He said: The Messenger of Allah (sw) said:
When the Sun sets, the gates of heaven and Paradise open and the supplications are accepted. So, blessed is he whose good deeds are lifted at that.
